narrative:
The model predicts you have a 61% chance of failing your final year, which is why the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. By far the strongest factor is that you have already failed one class in the past. Among students who passed, the average number of past failures is zero, so this history strongly pushes the model toward expecting you to fail again. Two other factors pulled the prediction slightly in the opposite direction. You have a clear desire to pursue higher education, something every student who passed also shared, which helps your chances. Additionally, you report having very low amounts of free time after school. While this might feel limiting, the model sees limited free time as a small positive signal compared with students who passed, perhaps because it suggests you are focused on responsibilities.

Despite these encouraging signs, your past academic setback outweighed them. To improve, you should focus on preventing another failure by seeking extra academic support early, creating a consistent study routine even if your free time is limited, and talking with your teachers about targeted help in the subjects that caused problems before. Taking the remedial courses seriously is a good first step toward changing this outlook.
